judged_text: loadUsers throws a generic 500 ('Unable to load users') for entirely user-controllable conditions — empty dynamicUserList on a dynamic group link and a non-array eventType.hosts — instead of a 4xx. A booker hitting a dynamic link whose user list resolves to empty (e.g. all hosts removed from the URL) gets a 500 Internal Server Error from the booking API rather than a 400/404, breaking the error contract and making client-side handling (which distinguishes 'no valid users' from server failure) impossible.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`, `loadUsers` now explicitly throws `new Error(...)` when `dynamicUserList` is not an array or is empty, and when `eventType.hosts` is not an array. Those errors are caught by the surrounding `try/catch`, but the `catch` only maps `HttpError` or `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` to a 400; all other errors (including these user/input-driven `Error`s) are converted into `new HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`. This matches the finding: empty/invalid user lists can yield a generic 500 instead of a 4xx, breaking the error contract for user-controllable conditions.
